title: Adria Arjona and the role of Celeste in Onslaught
seoTitle: Adria Arjona in A24 Horror Movie Onslaught
subtitle: The performance of the combat veteran in an A24 horror film
excerpt: Adria Arjona plays Celeste, a former combat veteran who manages a trailer park and faces heavily armed soldiers in Adam Wingard and Simon's Onslaught.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Adria Arjona takes on the role of Celeste, a combat veteran who manages a trailer park and lives with her daughter Daisy, played by Blake Kennedy. In Onslaught, Arjona's character finds herself caught up in a plot that blends extreme violence and social critique, marked by the presence of super-armed soldiers created in a secret laboratory.

What changes in the plot when Celeste enters the scene

At the beginning of the film, the scene opens with cuts between Celeste and another character, while chronicling the descent toward a future event. Celeste, despite caring for her daughter on a weekend that was supposed to be dedicated to the father, faces the threat of soldiers who have become killing machines. Arjona's presence brings a contrast between her character's physical strength and the vulnerability of her family environment.

How A24's production influences the style of Onslaught

A24 released the film over Labor Day weekend, when North American audiences are usually distracted by back-to-school plans and end-of-season barbecues. The studio has a history of supporting projects with a "grindhouse" aesthetic and controversial content, and Onslaught follows this line with explicit violence and the use of offensive language.

The super-soldier plot and the connection to Celeste

The plot involves a Nazi scientist, Hans, who creates three super-armed soldiers in a secret complex. After a massacre at a truck stop, the soldiers attack Celeste's trailer park, and one of them shares a past with her, heightening the narrative tension.

Arjona's role in critiquing the horror genre

By playing Celeste, Arjona contributes to the critique of the horror genre, which frequently features problematic portrayals of women. The film presents an approach that, according to critics, fails to overcome the lack of subplot development and the lack of tension in the final confrontations.

Production team and supporting cast

  • Director: Adam Wingard
  • Writers: Simon Barrett, Adam Wingard
  • Supporting cast: Reginald VelJohnson, Eric Wareheim, Michael Biehn
  • Cinematography: Oren Soffer
  • Production design: Tom Hammock
  • Editing: Josh Schaeffer, Adam Avery

The 92-minute film was produced by A24, RPC, and Breakaway Civilization, and features collaboration from executives such as David Kern and Jon Rosenberg.

With information from The Film Verdict.
